step1_summary.chief_complaint: Difficulty breathing after a recent bee/wasp sting; local rash at sting site; sensation of mild lip swelling and 'weird' tongue.

symptoms.severity_course: Patient feels anxious; does not feel acutely breathless now. Doctor observes normal breathing.
symptoms.location: Sting on arm with localized redness and puncture mark.
symptoms.associated: Subjective mild right-sided lip swelling; tongue feels odd. No visible lip swelling on video. No wheeze/stridor reported. No generalized hives, GI symptoms, or syncope reported.
symptoms.aggravating_alleviating: No medications taken yet; antihistamines advised.

medications_allergies.current_meds: None taken for this episode yet.

family_social_history.social: 27-year-old male; computer scientist; lives alone; has a cat.

exam: Video: breathing appears normal; speech unaffected.
Lips not visibly swollen; oropharyngeal view unremarkable.
Arm: localized slight redness/blotchiness with puncture mark; no notable swelling.

I: Cellulitis at sting site (very early consideration): Minutes after sting with localized erythema; however infection typically evolves over 24–72 hours and area is not hot or significantly swollen.
Large local inflammatory reaction to Hymenoptera sting: Local erythema and puncture mark consistent with expected inflammatory response.
I2: Toxic (non–IgE-mediated) reaction to Hymenoptera venom: Can cause local pain/erythema without systemic features; fits localized findings.
C: Hereditary angioedema (C1 inhibitor deficiency): Can cause lip/tongue swelling without urticaria, often triggered by minor trauma; less likely given no prior episodes and onset immediately after sting with no visible swelling.
A: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to Hymenoptera sting: Trigger temporal relationship, reports of dyspnea and lip/tongue sensations; but no objective airway compromise noted.
Histaminergic angioedema (allergic): Subjective lip/tongue swelling sensation post-sting; would often present with visible swelling or urticaria.
T: Local traumatic reaction to sting: Puncture with mild localized redness; explains local symptoms well.
E: Hyperventilation syndrome due to anxiety/panic: Acute stressor (sting), history of panic; observed normal breathing with subjective dyspnea suggests psychogenic component.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to Hymenoptera sting
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Immediate localized erythema and puncture mark with minimal swelling and no objective airway involvement are classic for a local reaction.
supporting_evidence: Localized arm redness/blotchiness at sting site with puncture mark
No visible lip/oropharyngeal swelling on video exam
opposing_evidence: Subjective lip/tongue sensations could suggest more than local reaction

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Early anaphylaxis (IgE-mediated systemic allergic reaction) to Hymenoptera sting
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Temporal link to sting with reports of dyspnea and oral sensations raises concern for systemic reaction, though objective findings are absent.
supporting_evidence: Subjective mild lip swelling and tongue feels 'weird'
Atopic background (eczema) modestly increases allergic risk
opposing_evidence: No visible lip/tongue swelling; normal oropharyngeal exam
Doctor observed normal breathing; no stridor/wheeze or voice change
No generalized urticaria, GI symptoms, hypotension, or syncope

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Acute stressor with patient-reported anxiety and normal observed respiration suggests psychogenic dyspnea.
supporting_evidence: Patient expresses being 'anxious' and sought reassurance
Clinician notes breathing appears normal and patient is speaking comfortably
opposing_evidence: Temporal association with sting could represent true allergic reaction
Subjective oral swelling sensation less typical for pure panic

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Subjective oral swelling could represent early angioedema, but lack of visible swelling and stability make this less likely.
supporting_evidence: Reports of lip swelling sensation and tongue feeling 'weird' after sting
opposing_evidence: No progression, no airway compromise, no urticaria

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Infection is uncommon within minutes of a sting and exam lacks warmth or spreading erythema.
opposing_evidence: Area not described as hot, tender, or expanding; no systemic signs
